clue.text: Source of hot air essential in a balloon

definitions.meaning: a windbag, someone who talks endlessly and emptily
the envelope holding the lifting gas is the vital part of a balloon

explanation.surface: A balloonist explains which part of the craft holds the hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are one word: a long-winded talker, and the fabric envelope that holds a balloon's gas.

clue.text: Put away Agassi's first service

indicators.note: the first letter of the tennis player's name is taken

parts.note: a Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: Andre Agassi puts away a point with his opening serve.
explanation.walkthrough: The tennis picture makes 'service' a serve; here it is a church Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away is to store up or accumulate, the sense of hoarding.

clue.text: Hundred drink in flat revel

indicators.note: the hundred and the drink go inside the word for flat

parts.note: flat, dull and banal are synonyms
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
cha is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone throws a party in their flat with a hundred drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' reads as an apartment but means dull; 'in' puts the hundred and the tea inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A drunken festivity, named after Bacchus, god of wine.

clue.text: Brilliant group of unknowns following carnival

indicators.note: the unknowns come after the carnival in the answer

parts.note: a gala is a festive carnival or fete
x is a standard algebraic unknown
y is the second standard algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A dazzling troupe of unheard-of performers turns up after the carnival.
explanation.walkthrough: In algebra X and Y are the usual unknowns, so 'unknowns' gives two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A starry cluster or a gathering of famous people is called this.

clue.text: He gets nailed fighting for title

indicators.note: the letters scrap and tumble about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A boxer gets nailed while fighting for a championship title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges HE and NAILED.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper story's heading is its title in large type.

clue.text: Look for unlikely outcome in comedian vs novelist

parts.note: Bob Hope was a famous American comedian
vs is short for versus, against
Anthony Hope wrote The Prisoner of Zenda

explanation.surface: A match is billed as comedian versus novelist, with an unlikely result expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Two famous Hopes, Bob the comedian and Anthony the novelist, sit either side of 'vs'.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to keep wishing for something even when it seems impossible.

clue.text: In some place or other, we hear; vaguely outside US city

indicators.note: the rearranged letters sit on either side of the city
the letters are given vaguely, not in exact order, so rearrange them

parts.note: NY is New York

explanation.surface: Someone says the place is somewhere vaguely outside an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' looks like a sound signal but is the fodder: 'vaguely' rearranges it to A WHERE, which goes 'outside' NY.
explanation.definitionFit: Means at any location at all, wherever it may be.

clue.text: A ruminant Latin priest

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist priest

explanation.surface: A Latin-speaking priest chews things over.
explanation.definitionFit: The South American camelid chews the cud, so it counts as a ruminant.

clue.text: A near type, you might say

definitions.text: A near type, you might say

parts.words: A near type, you might say
parts.note: someone living close by is a near type; read in sound, a horse that whinnies is a neigh-er, so the word splits as a horse noise plus a boring person

explanation.walkthrough: Said out loud, the word sounds like a horse's cry followed by a dull person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living close at hand, the person next door.

clue.text: Sleeping sickness?

parts.note: not the tropical fever but a disorder in which the sufferer falls asleep without warning

explanation.walkthrough: The phrase normally names a tropical disease; the question mark points to a condition of sudden sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A neurological disorder causing sudden uncontrollable bouts of sleep.

clue.text: Drug knocked back during medication…

indicators.note: the letters are read backwards, knocked back the way a drink is
the answer sits inside the word that follows

explanation.surface: Someone knocks back a drug while on medication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' takes DICA from inside meDICAtion; 'knocked back' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for LSD, the hallucinogen.

clue.text: … like an oral drug dose given to one with a respiratory problem

parts.note: as means like, in comparisons

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for a drug dose is said aloud and respelt

parts.note: a fix is an addict's dose of a drug
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone with breathing trouble is given a drug to take by mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oral' suggests swallowing a pill; it actually says FIX is heard, spelt PHYX.
explanation.definitionFit: Suffocation from lack of oxygen is a breathing disorder.

clue.text: More than one fell hard in races

indicators.note: the hard letter goes inside the word for races

parts.note: heats are qualifying races
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Several runners fell hard during the races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fell' reads as the verb to fall; here it is a noun, a stretch of upland moor.
explanation.definitionFit: A fell is open upland moor, so several of them are stretches of moorland.

clue.text: Devotee embracing universal deity

indicators.note: the fan wraps around the universal letter

parts.note: a fan is a devotee
U is the film-rating abbreviation for universal

explanation.surface: A worshipper embraces a god of all things.
explanation.definitionFit: A rural god of Roman myth, half man half goat.

clue.text: Feel nauseated? It sickens me in a boat

indicators.note: the letters are made sick and churned up, so rearrange them

explanation.surface: A seasick passenger complains that being on a boat turns their stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sickens' rearranges ME IN A BOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: To loathe something is to be disgusted by it, figuratively sickened.

clue.text: Cause of sparkle, a measure round edge of bonfire

indicators.note: the a and the measure go round the letter taken from bonfire

parts.note: a ration is a measured allowance

indicators.note: the last letter of the word bonfire, its trailing edge

explanation.surface: A measured portion is set round the edge of a bonfire to make it sparkle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge of' takes the final letter of bonfire, not its first; A plus RATION goes 'round' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Charging a drink with gas is what makes it fizz and sparkle.

clue.text: I settle on fancy roofing piece

indicators.note: fancy means elaborately reworked, so rearrange the letters

explanation.surface: A builder decides on a fancy piece for the roof.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges I SETTLE ON.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat slab of stone used like a tile to cover roofs.

clue.text: Easily handled pieces captured by one like a master

indicators.note: the pieces are held inside the other letters

parts.note: a means one
able means skilled, as a master is
men are chess or draughts pieces

explanation.surface: A chess master captures pieces with ease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pieces' are chessmen, matching the master in the surface; 'captured by' sets them inside the other letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone compliant and tractable is easy to manage.

clue.text: Count shows head Liberal, a notable, returned

parts.note: nob is slang for head

indicators.note: the notable is turned back to front

parts.note: a name is a notable, a celebrity

explanation.surface: A count shows that the Liberal leader, a notable figure, was re-elected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb but is the nobleman; 'returned' turns only the notable around, not the head or the Liberal.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a European aristocrat of rank.

clue.text: Box with left leading — that's the trick

indicators.note: the left letter comes in front of the box

parts.note: an ark is a chest or box

explanation.surface: Boxing with your left leading is the trick of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' reads as a verb from boxing; it is a noun, ARK, a chest.
explanation.definitionFit: A prank or bit of fun mischief.

clue.text: What repeatedly goes down, then up?

definitions.text: What repeatedly goes down, then up?

parts.words: What repeatedly goes down, then up?
parts.note: an eight-legged creature lowers itself on its thread and climbs back up, again and again

explanation.walkthrough: The riddle suggests a yo-yo; the creature in mind drops on silk and climbs back up.
explanation.definitionFit: Arachnids descend on a strand of silk and climb back.

clue.text: Bird after endless pests in plant

indicators.note: the last letter of the pests is cut off

parts.note: lice are pests
a hen is a bird

explanation.surface: A bird feeds on pests in the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: An organism of fungus and alga often classed with simple plants.

clue.text: Poet in Russia

parts.note: at home means in
R stands for Russia

explanation.surface: A poet lives in Russia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a link but supplies HOME (being in means at home).
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek author of the Iliad and the Odyssey.

clue.text: Records judge confirming a hanging

parts.note: tapes are recordings
to try a case is to judge it

explanation.surface: Court records show the judge confirming a death by hanging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a hanging' sounds like an execution; it is a wall hanging.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall decoration is hung on a wall.

clue.text: Travel with compass

definitions.meaning: the reach or scope of something

explanation.definitionFit: One word means to wander freely and also the scope or extent of something.

clue.text: Tree in bud before onset of May

parts.note: bud, short for buddy, means pal

indicators.note: the first letter of the month

explanation.surface: A tree is in bud before May arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bud' reads as a shoot on a tree; it is a buddy, PAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A tropical tree with a crown of large leaves.

clue.text: Dog with leap bagging game on edges of moorland stretch

annotationWithheld.why: Dog with leap bagging game on edges of moorland stretch: BOUND round LOO gives B-LOO-OUND, but nothing in 'on edges of moorland stretch' gives the D and H needed (edges of moorland is MD); likely OCR garble with no scan
annotationWithheld.clue: Dog with leap bagging game on edges of moorland stretch

clue.text: Stay continually put back to secure rickety pier

indicators.note: the reversed word holds the shaky pier inside it
the word for continually is read backwards

parts.note: ever means always, continually

indicators.note: rickety means shaky, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rickety pier is kept up for a while by being shored up again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses EVER to REVE; 'rickety' rearranges PIER into PRIE, which it secures.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay of execution is a postponement or pardon.

clue.text: European in check jacket

indicators.note: the European letter sits inside the check

parts.note: to refer to a source is to check it

explanation.surface: A European wears a checked jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'check' suggests a pattern; it is the verb refer.
explanation.definitionFit: A short thick double-breasted jacket worn by sailors.
